audit.whatIsWrong: The early-game text says 'a level 1 Blinding Dart cancels any trade you try to start', which flatly contradicts whys[0], the TL;DR and the Key Ability Interactions block in the same matchup, all of which correctly say the blind does not stop Flamespitter.
audit.why: This is the defining interaction of the lane and the file argues both sides of it. A Rumble reading the early paragraph backs off exactly when he should walk in.
audit.corrected: Level 1 is thin because Teemo out-ranges you and Toxic Shot chips, not because of the blind. Blinding Dart removes your autos only — Flamespitter burns through it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Blinding Dart: blinds the target, an auto-attack effect)
champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (Flamespitter is a spell, not an auto)

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike says Liandry's burn is something Teemo 'cannot just shield through', and whys[5] repeats 'cannot simply shield through'. Teemo has no shield in his kit.
audit.why: A fabricated defensive ability changes how a player values the spike — you brace for a shield that never appears and misread why the burn works.
audit.corrected: The first-item spike works because Liandry's burn keeps ticking while he kites; the thing he actually escapes with is Move Quick (W), on 14s.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] credits Equalizer's slow with punishing 'his lack of a real escape tool'. Teemo's Move Quick (W) is exactly that — a passive move-speed buff plus an active sprint on a 14s cooldown. Separately, Blinding Dart's flat 7s cooldown at every rank is never given, despite the whole matchup being built on tracking it.
audit.why: Point 4 is the key point. Two concrete, checkable facts were available in the kit and neither reached the page, while a false absence was asserted in place of one of them.
audit.corrected: State it as it is: Blinding Dart is 7s flat at all ranks, so the window is predictable; Move Quick is a real 14s disengage, and Equalizer's slow is what beats it. Toxic Shot (E) is on-hit magic damage, so armour misreads these trades — his chip scales with attack speed.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Blinding Dart cd 7 flat; Move Quick cd 14; Toxic Shot onHit)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing records that Rumble's Scrap Shield has no displacement component.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json claims 'Both sides carry displacement (Scrap Shield (W) vs Noxious Trap (R))' for this matchup. Riot's Scrap Shield description is a shield plus a move-speed burst, with no knockup; the derived flag misfired.
audit.corrected: No edit made — flagged so the false displacement line is not written in.

edits.before: At level 1 Teemo out-ranges you completely — his auto-attack plus poison chip will win if you stand in it, and a level 1 Blinding Dart cancels any trade you try to start. Accept a thin early game: last-hit at the tip of Flamespitter range and do not commit to him before you have Electro-Harpoon. At level 2 the matchup opens — double Electro-Harpoon into Danger Zone Flamespitter can halve his health bar in one go, but only fire it after his Blinding Dart is visibly on cooldown. Level 3 is your best early window: full kit online means if he overextends for a wave you can E-E slow, walk Q through him, and shield the return poke with W. Force him to respect your heat window or pay for it.
edits.after: At level 1 Teemo out-ranges you completely — his auto plus Toxic Shot poison chips you down if you stand in it, but Blinding Dart never touches Flamespitter; it only removes your autos. Accept a thin early game: last-hit at the tip of Flamespitter range and do not commit to him before you have Electro-Harpoon. At level 2 the matchup opens — double Electro-Harpoon into Danger Zone Flamespitter can halve his health bar in one go, and his dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank, so you can count it out loud. Level 3 is your best early window: full kit online means if he overextends for a wave you can E-E slow, walk Q through him, and shield the return poke with W.

edits.after: Liandry's Torment plus Danger Zone Q becomes a sustained burn that keeps ticking while he kites, and your Equalizer finally threatens a solo kill.

edits.before: Liandry's Torment turns Danger Zone Flamespitter into a sustained burn he cannot simply shield through, making the first-item window your most reliable solo-kill opportunity.
edits.after: Liandry's Torment turns Danger Zone Flamespitter into a burn that keeps ticking through a Move Quick escape, making the first-item window your best solo-kill chance.

edits.before: Equalizer changes the threat geometry — you no longer need to close distance to create a kill window, and its slow punishes his lack of a real escape tool.
edits.after: Equalizer changes the threat geometry — you no longer need to close distance to make a kill window, and its slow is what beats Move Quick, his 14-second sprint.

edits.before: Bait Blinding Dart off a minion trade, then immediately enter Danger Zone and walk Flamespitter through him
edits.after: Walk Flamespitter through him even while blinded — the dart takes your autos, never your Q, and it is 7s flat

edits.before: Track Teemo's Blinding Dart: Blinds autos — NOT your flamespitter. When it is down — Flame + E-R him.
edits.after: Blinding Dart blinds autos, never Flamespitter, and is a flat 7s at every rank. Move Quick is his 14s out.

notes: The most valuable fix here was not a wrong ability name — the names are all correct, and both packet suspectNames ('Drop Equalizer', 'Use the Equalizer') are false positives. The real defect is that champ-data/content/rumble.js argues both sides of the lane's defining interaction: the early paragraph says Blinding Dart 'cancels any trade you try to start' while whys[0], the TL;DR and Key Ability Interactions all correctly say the blind does not touch Flamespitter. Separately, 'shield through' appears twice for a champion with no shield. Worth checking whether that phrase is boilerplate reused across other Rumble matchups against shieldless enemies.
